reviewFindings.fact: All distinct main/test input paths are hashed before the first Remote invocation or upload. Frozen dictionary is never rewritten after local rebuild. A local file changed before/during upload must fail later remote comparison rather than inherit a new local identity.

Each unique uploaded path is checked using remote Get-FileHash and compared to the preupload frozen digest; successful identity is appended to uploadedArtifacts. Main exeSha256 comes from frozen input, not a later local read.

PowerShell hashes exact remote test path and compares frozen expected digest before invoking it. The same digest is returned as binarySha256 alongside output/exitCode. Python compares that field again before appending report/PASS. Removed postexecution local hashing cannot relabel old remote bytes as a newer local artifact.

Upload, pretest remote and returned digest mismatches raise rather than PASS. Existing try/finally own-marker cleanup, timeout log handling and SSH authorization retention remain unchanged. No extra scheduled task, scope or privilege added by this diff.

Remote pre-execution hash is evidence for the own isolated file under exclusive test operation. It is not a locked-open handle/hash attestation of immutable mapped image against adversarial remote file replacement between hashing and process launch. Such an adversary is outside this change and no stronger guarantee is claimed.
